sam_py: quick heads-up — discovered a weird pyright/mypy mismatch with the autogenerated python models in the sampleapp.

sam_py: repro steps: generate SDK from latest spec, import client, then mypy/pyright complains on call sites where a param is annotated as `str | None` in the generated model constructor but docstring and runtime accept None fine.

sam_py: minimal repro below:
```python
# example.py
from my_sdk import Client, CreateThingRequest

client = Client()
req = CreateThingRequest(name=None)  # allowed at runtime
client.create_thing(req)
```

sam_py: pyright output: `error: Argument of type "None" cannot be assigned to parameter "name" of type "str | None"` — this only shows up when running pyright with older python target or certain config. mypy also flags in some configs.

maria_devex: thanks for the repro, ugh. do you have the exact generated snippet? is it using `from __future__ import annotations`? that often changes how union types are emitted.

sam_py: yes, grabbed the generated model file. top of file does NOT include `from __future__ import annotations`. snippet: 
```python
class CreateThingRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None

    def __init__(self, name: str | None = None):
        super().__init__(name=name)
```

sam_py: runtime works (tests pass) but static checkers choke depending on pyright config and pythonVersion ts.

leo_backend: hmm — when we emit `str | None` without future annotations pyright might evaluate those at import time; for pyright/pylance combos that target <3.10 semantics it can be brittle. two options: (1) always emit `from __future__ import annotations` at the top of generated files so unions are forward refs, (2) fallback to `Optional[str]`/`typing.Optional` which is more compatible.

leo_backend: also noticed our gen pipeline sometimes mixes `list[str]` and `Sequence[str]` in different places which makes narrow type inference inconsistent for clients.

maria_devex: agreed — actionable plan: add `from __future__ import annotations` to generator templates by default, and add a generator option `--legacy-typing` that switches unions to `Optional[...]` and `typing.List[...]` for older toolchains. will also add a note in sampleapp README about recommended pyright/mypy config (pythonVersion >= 3.10 or enable "useLibraryCodeForTypes").

sam_py: nice. any quick workaround I can patch locally?

leo_backend: temp workaround in your project: in pyrightconfig.json set "pythonVersion": "3.10" (or 3.11), or add `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on the call sites. worst-case, pin generated package to a patched local wheel with future import added.

maria_devex: I'll open a generator PR, add test that runs pyright on a tiny generated package so we catch regressions. sam, can you paste the exact pyright config that flagged it? will help reproduce in CI.

sam_py: here's my pyrightconfig.json: 
```json
{
  "typeCheckingMode": "basic",
  "pythonVersion": "3.9",
  "reportGeneralTypeIssues": true
}
```

sam_py: lowering pythonVersion to 3.9 was part of our monorepo target, which is why this slipped by.

maria_devex: perfect, thanks. will target a generator patch that handles both cases.

ci-bot: created issue RED-4207 in repo "sdk-gen" and attached repro files (sam_py). Labels: devex, typing, pyright. https://redwood.example/RED-4207

maria_devex: assigning to @leo_backend for implementation, will add unit + pyright check in CI. patch plan: 1) emit future annotations by default, 2) add generator flag `--compat-typing` for Optional/List fallbacks, 3) update sampleapp README.

leo_backend: ack, I'll pick it up tomorrow; will post the PR link here.

sam_py: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
